classes.name: General elections to the National Parliament
classes.name_en: National Parliament general elections (Legislative Assembly in 1976)
classes.finest_note: Each returning officer's gazetted notice gives one constituency's candidate votes, rejected votes, electors who voted, and registered electors; no polling-station figures are published.
classes.note: First past the post in single-member constituencies: 38 from 1976, 47 from 1993, and 50 since 1997. The Legislative Assembly elected in 1976 became the National Parliament at independence on 7 July 1978, and the Parliament numbers it as the first; the 2024 Parliament is the twelfth. Parliament runs four years from its first sitting unless dissolved sooner (Constitution s.73); the Constitution (Amendment) Act 2022 suspended s.73(3) and dissolved the eleventh Parliament on 31 December 2023, and the 2024 election was the first held jointly with the provincial assembly and Honiara City Council elections.

classes.name: Ordinary elections to the provincial assemblies
classes.finest_note: Each returning officer's notice gives one ward's candidate votes, rejected votes, electors who voted, and registered electors.
classes.note: Each of the nine provincial assemblies is elected by first past the post in single-member wards (Provincial Government Act 1997 s.7), 173 in all. Until 2024 each assembly kept its own cycle, an ordinary election falling on the fourth anniversary of the last (s.9). The Provincial Government (Amendment) Act 2023 moved seven assemblies to the 2024 joint election and Choiseul and Western, elected in December 2022, to the same day in 2028. The assemblies were created by the Provincial Government Act 1981; the 1996 Act briefly replaced them in Temotu, Isabel, and Central with area assemblies and provincial councils.

cadence.locator: https://www.mpgis.gov.sb/legislation/6-provincial-government-act-1997.html (s.9(1): "an ordinary election of members of a Provincial Assembly shall be held on the fourth anniversary of the date of the office of previous election")

classes.name: Ordinary elections to the Honiara City Council
classes.finest_note: Each returning officer's notice gives one ward's candidate votes, rejected votes, electors who voted, and registered electors.
classes.note: The elected members of the council are returned by single-member wards, 12 since at least 2024, by first past the post; the council also has appointed and ex officio members. An ordinary election fell on the fourth anniversary of the last (Honiara City Act 1999 s.6(3)) until the Honiara City (Amendment) Act 2023 moved it to the 2024 joint election.

classes.name: Honiara Town Council elections
classes.note: Before the Honiara City Act 1999 Honiara was governed as a town council under the Local Government Act (Cap. 14); the 1997 index lists a notice of Honiara Town elections.
classes.disposition_reason: Results were printed only in the Solomon Islands Gazette, which is not online; no official publication of the town council polls has been reached.

classes.name: Area assembly elections under the Provincial Government Act 1996
classes.note: The Provincial Government Act 1996 replaced the provincial assemblies with area assemblies and provincial councils; area assemblies were elected in Temotu, Isabel, and Central in 1996-1997 before the Provincial Government Act 1997 restored the assemblies (the 1996 and 1997 indexes list returning officers for area assembly elections in every province).
classes.disposition_reason: Results were printed only in the Solomon Islands Gazette, which is not online.

classes.name: Area council elections
classes.note: Area councils sat below the provinces under the Provincial Government Act 1981; the 1997 Act kept them only until new assemblies were elected and left area councils to provincial ordinance, and none is elected today.
classes.disposition_reason: No official record of area council elections has been reached; any results were local notices, not gazetted results.

classes.name: Governing Council elections
classes.note: In 1970 the Legislative and Executive Councils were replaced by a Governing Council with elected members, elected in 1970 and 1973, and replaced by the Legislative Assembly in 1974.
classes.disposition_reason: Protectorate-era returns survive only in colonial gazettes and reports; no official body publishes them online.

dates.note: Governing Council election; the date is not quoted from a fetched official source.
Governing Council election; the date is not quoted from a fetched official source.

classes.name: Legislative Council elections
classes.note: The Advisory Council became the Legislative Council in 1960; its first elected members were returned in 1964 and 1967, partly by direct vote and partly through local councils acting as electoral colleges.
classes.disposition_reason: Protectorate-era returns survive only in colonial gazettes and reports; no official body publishes them online.

dates.note: The first Legislative Council election with elected members; the date is not quoted from a fetched official source.
Legislative Council election; the date is not quoted from a fetched official source.

classes.name: Election of the Governor-General by Parliament
classes.disposition_reason: The Governor-General represents the King and is chosen by a vote of the members of Parliament before appointment (Constitution s.27 and Schedule 1); there is no public vote.

classes.name: Election of the Prime Minister by Parliament
classes.locator: https://solomons.gov.sb/ministry-of-justice-and-legal-affairs/attorney-generals-chambers/annual-indexes-of-gazette-notices-and-legal-notices/2024-annual-index-to-gazette-and-legal-notices/ (Gazette 74, notice 641: "Notification of the Election of the Prime Minister")
classes.disposition_reason: The Prime Minister is elected by the members of Parliament from among themselves (Constitution s.33 and Schedule 2), and the result is gazetted; there is no public vote.

classes.name: Election of provincial premiers by the assemblies
classes.disposition_reason: Each premier is elected by secret ballot by an absolute majority of the provincial assembly (Provincial Government Act 1997 s.20(2)), and the result is gazetted; there is no public vote.

classes.name: Election of the Mayor of Honiara by the City Council
classes.disposition_reason: The City Council elects the Mayor from its elected members within fourteen days of an ordinary election (Honiara City Act 1999 s.7(1)); there is no public vote.

classes.name: National referendums
classes.locator: https://parliament.gov.sb/business/acts/files/2022/Constitution%20(Amendment)%20Act%202022.pdf ("This Act alters the Constitution under section 61(5)(b)(iii) and (iv) of the Constitution")
classes.disposition_reason: The Constitution provides no referendum: it is altered by Act of Parliament under s.61, and no national vote has been held. A referendum would be a new class.

classes.name: Judges and magistrates
classes.disposition_reason: Judges and magistrates are appointed by the Governor-General under the Constitution, on the advice of the Prime Minister or of the Judicial and Legal Service Commission; none is elected.

classes.name: Party candidate selections
classes.disposition_reason: Parties registered under the Political Parties Integrity Act 2014 choose their candidates by their own rules; the state neither runs nor publishes the selections, and candidates enter the official process at nomination.
